MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Testing for genetic susceptibility to BRCA-related cancer.

METHODOLOGY
Bidirectional DNA sequencing and Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) analysis of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes.

Sequencing: Complete analysis of all coding exons and intron-exon boundaries of BRCA1 (NM_007294.3) and BRCA2 (NM_000059.3) genes. Bidirectional Sanger sequencing provides >99% detection sensitivity for point mutations and small insertions/deletions.

MLPA: Analysis performed using GeneScreen-C1 kit for BRCA1 exons 1A-24 and GeneDetect-B2 kit for BRCA2 exons 1-27. This technique detects large deletions and duplications not identifiable by sequencing.

Combined detection rate: >98% of all known pathogenic BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations.

RESULTS

BRCA1 (GenBank U14680.1):
No pathogenic mutations detected
All 24 exons successfully sequenced
No large deletions or duplications detected by MLPA

BRCA2 (GenBank U43746.1):
No pathogenic mutations detected
All 27 exons successfully sequenced
No large deletions or duplications detected by MLPA

Nomenclature: Based on GenBank reference sequences U14680.1 (BRCA1) and U43746.1 (BRCA2), with nucleotide position 1 corresponding to the first base of the translation initiation codon.

SUMMARY
No pathogenic mutations were identified in either BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes. Based on these results, the patient is very unlikely to have a pathogenic mutation in the BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes.

TECHNICAL NOTES
1. This test detects >98% of pathogenic mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes
2. Rare mutations in regulatory regions or deep intronic sequences may not be detected
3. This test does not detect mutations in other genes associated with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
4. Genetic variants of uncertain significance (VUS) are reported separately if identified
5. Testing limitations include inability to detect certain mutation types such as inversions or complex rearrangements

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
